![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/5a661c340c9eb953b93ceeebb23cd3d251a5591db3893a917f94f465c81bbffc.png)

Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m∠1.$
question.worked_solution:
Consider $∠2$ and $∠3$ in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/db08637378dcf3968cb0e526057212d7c673fb1818eb84db5f076eb9cf4fb2c9.png)

Note that $∠2$ and the angle whose measure is ${110}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠2={110}^{∘}.
$$

Similarly, note that $∠3$ and the angle whose measure is ${45}^{∘}$ are corresponding angles formed by the same transversal. Therefore, 

$$
m∠3={45}^{∘}.
$$

Let's add these measures to our diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14178066/assets/9420706692d49a3faf575d20be6b64f306d9fc901e477184e6b2f2ad21907d8f.png)

The angles $∠1$, $∠2,$ and $∠3$ combined give a straight angle. So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠1+m∠2+m∠3 & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{110}^{∘}+{45}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1+{155}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠1 & ={25}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
